1) Allies get burned when they loose their life points. Talaq has 1 life
and strikes with Blood Sweat. Is the opponent damaged?

2) Talbot's chainsaw VtES text: "(...) minion may attack others as a +1
stealth action, presses to continue combat on the 1st round and (...)".
What are these "presses"? Does this mean the minion must press once on the
1st round or that it has unlimited presses on the 1st round?

effect (since it's not aggravated)?

3) Gas Powered Chainsaw has a rather different wording from the one on
Sawed-off Shotgun, though they resemble one another (give or take ranged
damage and a pool). The difference is that on GPC, it states "this weapon
can inflict 3 damage per combat", and SOS says "only usable once per
combat". Does this mean that if I strike with one of these and the opponen
dodges I could still use the GPS again whereas the SOS is unusable? What
if damage is prevented, does the wording on GPS imply that I could strike
again for the amount of prevented damage?

4) What exactly does the card "Justicar Retribution" do? When does a
vampire has a "permanent bleed score of 3 or more" under standart set
cards (I realize with Legendary vampire this is possible, but I can't
imagine other ways). Are ICs affected? (guess not)

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
David Pontes wrote:
> 1) Allies get burned when they loose their life points. Talaq has 1 life
> and strikes with Blood Sweat. Is the opponent damaged?

Not from the strike, since Talaq is burned (and combat ended) before
strike resolution.

> 2) Talbot's chainsaw VtES text: "(...) minion may attack others as a +1
> stealth action, presses to continue combat on the 1st round and (...)".
> What are these "presses"? Does this mean the minion must press once on the
> 1st round or that it has unlimited presses on the 1st round?

It is a convoluted sentence. The "presses" is a present-perfect
verb tense of press, used (in this case) to indicate that the
bearer of Talbot's automatically presses on the first round of
the Talbot-given-attack-action.

> Also, can the damage from Talbot's Cs be put on Ambrosius to no
> effect (since it's not aggravated)?

Correct, Ambrosius can receive and ignore the untap-phase damage of
Talbot's Chainsaw.

> 3) Gas Powered Chainsaw has a rather different wording from the one on
> Sawed-off Shotgun, though they resemble one another (give or take ranged
> damage and a pool). The difference is that on GPC, it states "this weapon
> can inflict 3 damage per combat", and SOS says "only usable once per
> combat". Does this mean that if I strike with one of these and the opponen
> dodges I could still use the GPS again whereas the SOS is unusable? What
> if damage is prevented, does the wording on GPS imply that I could strike
> again for the amount of prevented damage?

The template on GPC should indicate that it is only usuable once per
combat, just like the Shotgun. The text from the WotC list (which
has been wrong in other places) is:

The minion with this equipment can inflict 3 damage as a strike
once each combat.

Where did you get your card text quote from?
If it's from the actual card (and the WotC list is in error), then
I'll pass the question on to the RT.
Otherwise, treat it like the above quote.

> 4) What exactly does the card "Justicar Retribution" do? When does a
> vampire has a "permanent bleed score of 3 or more" under standart set
> cards (I realize with Legendary vampire this is possible, but I can't
> imagine other ways). Are ICs affected? (guess not)

Get Ozmo with Tasha Morgan.
Or any vampire who has perfomed a Pulse of the Canaille.
ICs are affected; they have base bleeds of 3.

Messages.Author: Boon Sian Chang
Messages.Body:
I'm sure this has been asked before but:

1) If normal and aggravated damage are done in the same round, who chooses
what damage gets applied first? Or is normal damage done first, then
aggravated, or vice versa?

2) Do dragon's breath rounds add 2 aggravated damage in addition to the
weapon's normal damage? Or does it make all damage from the weapon
aggravated?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Boon Sian Chang wrote:
> 1) If normal and aggravated damage are done in the same round, who chooses
> what damage gets applied first? Or is normal damage done first, then
> aggravated, or vice versa?

When a mix of aggravated and normal damage is done at the same
time, the vampire must burn blood to heal the normal damage before
dealing with the aggravated damage (thereby maximizing the chances
of burning a vampire).

> 2) Do dragon's breath rounds add 2 aggravated damage in addition to the
> weapon's normal damage? Or does it make all damage from the weapon
> aggravated?

It adds two aggravated to the weapon's normal damage.

Messages.Author: Samuel Lacas
Messages.Body:
1- "The Barrens" allows to "tap to discard a card". Is there a ruling
about WHEN tapping is allowed, or can it be used at any time ?
(out-of-turn, during a combat, etc.)

2- If a vampire tries to get himself or someone else out of Torpor, are
the two blood points spent even if the action is blocked ?

sL

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Samuel Lacas wrote:
>
> 1- "The Barrens" allows to "tap to discard a card". Is there a ruling
> about WHEN tapping is allowed, or can it be used at any time ?
> (out-of-turn, during a combat, etc.)

It can be used at any time.

> 2- If a vampire tries to get himself or someone else out of Torpor, are
> the two blood points spent even if the action is blocked ?

No. The blood is spent only if the action is successful.



Messages.Author: J. Andrew Lipscomb
Messages.Body:
In article <73d8r17...@cohen.logique.jussieu.fr>, Samuel Lacas
<la...@cohen.logique.jussieu.fr> wrote:

> 2- If a vampire tries to get himself or someone else out of Torpor, are
> the two blood points spent even if the action is blocked ?

No. Blood cost of an action is only paid if it succeeds (Tereza Rostas's
Edge theft is an exception to the rule).
